title: Abdominal Tics in Children and Adolescents: A Phenomenology-First Diagnostic Framework and Differential Diagnosis.
Abdominal Tics in Children and Adolescents: A Phenomenology‐First Diagnostic Framework and Differential Diagnosis

population_scope: Children/adolescents; no new participant cohort and no severe-adult efficacy estimate.
study_type: Clinically focused narrative synthesis, not primary research.
source_access: PubMed abstract and metadata inspected transiently; Crossref metadata corroborated dates. No full-text assessment.
original_summary: Proposes a differential-diagnosis framework for abdominal tic-like movements. No original controlled comparison or validated diagnostic accuracy is established by this review.
screening_decision: Newly encountered pediatric narrative review, electronic October 16 and PubMed entry October 17. Abstract assessed as secondary synthesis; exclude from primary-study evidence and do not treat proposed diagnostic framework as validated clinical accuracy.
correction_retraction_check: No linked PubMed notice; Crossref update-to empty at retrieval. This is limited metadata screening, not comprehensive clearance.
cohort_deduplication: No new cohort; reviewed studies are not counted again as original data.
next_step: Retain as secondary context only; reconsider if new primary validation or a material correction appears.
